conf.description: Palo Alto NGFW Threat log (json over HTTP, PAN-OS 10.2/11.1), direct route: structural JSON extract only. Field-level ECS mapping is deliberately NOT implemented - the work order's own fields_omitted note states the HTTP Payload Format template's key names are operator-chosen, not vendor-fixed, so no rename/eval can be written without guessing key names.

conf.comment: Palo Alto NGFW Threat log, json format over an HTTP Source, direct route. The work order's fields[] is empty and fields_omitted explains why: whoever configures the HTTP Server Profile's Payload Format for the Threat log type chooses the JSON attribute names, so this inventory is operator-defined rather than vendor-fixed. Per the brief's rule against guessing unguessable field names, this pipeline only performs the structural work that is true regardless of key names - extracting the JSON body and tagging event.dataset - and leaves ECS mapping as a documented gap until the real payload template is pinned. Once the template is known, apply the same threatid-split and severity-lookup logic as the syslog-csv format in this directory.

functions.description: Record why field-level mapping is out of scope for this format

Best-effort timestamp detection over the raw JSON text, since no specific timestamp key name is known for this operator-defined template
